PMID:41476023.topic: Supracondylar fracture management against appropriate use criteria
PMID:41476023.setting: Mansoura University Emergency Hospital, a tertiary referral centre in the Nile Delta
PMID:41476023.standard: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS) appropriate use criteria (AUC) for paediatric supracondylar humerus fractures; primary outcome proportion of cases managed 'appropriately'

cycle1.result: 62.1% (36/58) managed 'appropriately'; 19.0% (11/58) 'rarely appropriate'; 19.0% (11/58) 'may be appropriate'. 65% of type IIa fractures were managed with casting alone ('rarely appropriate').

PMID:41476023.intervention: Cycle 2: mandatory 2-hour AUC workshop, pocket reference cards and a departmental protocol with a type II fracture flowchart. Cycle 3: three refresher workshops, AUC training in resident orientation, laminated AUC flowcharts in ED, theatre and ward, departmental grand round presentations, weekly case discussions and individualised audit feedback.

cycle2.result: 87.9% (51/58) managed 'appropriately' (25.8% absolute improvement from baseline); 'rarely appropriate' 3.4% (2/58); 'may be appropriate' 8.6% (5/58). AUC tool use documented in over 95% of cases.

PMID:41476023.other_findings: Intermediate cycle (September 2021–February 2022, n=62) showed 75.8% (47/62) appropriate and 9.7% (6/62) rarely appropriate, with AUC rating documented in only 45% of cases. At baseline 78% of surgeons were unfamiliar with the AUC web tool.

PMID:34632079.topic: Virtual fracture clinic referral and remote follow-up
PMID:34632079.setting: OLVG, a level 2 trauma centre and teaching hospital in Amsterdam (emergency department and virtual fracture clinic)
PMID:34632079.standard: Predefined standards from national coronavirus outpatient guidelines and local consensus: (1) all eligible ED trauma patients referred for VFC review; (2) all patients contacted after VFC review; (3) patient-initiated follow-up by default where possible; (4) follow-up by telephone or video where possible. Target 100% for standard 1.

cycle1.result: 162/184 (88.0%) referred for VFC review; 98.1% reached afterwards (3 patients, 1.9%, not reached); 29/162 (17.9%) discharged 'virtually'; 137/291 (45.0%) appointments remote. Median total ED time 95 minutes vs 131 minutes at baseline (p<0.001).

PMID:34632079.intervention: After an evaluation meeting, ED staff were invited to attend VFC review for direct feedback, presentations explaining the workflow were held, posters were put up in the ED, and a patient information leaflet asking patients to call if not contacted by 15:00 the next workday was introduced.

cycle2.result: 302/305 (98.4%) referred for VFC review; 99.0% reached afterwards (3 patients, 1.0%, not reached); 41/302 (13.6%) discharged 'virtually'; 179/436 (41.1%) appointments remote. Median total ED time 98 minutes (−33 minutes vs baseline, p=0.001); time to review 47 minutes (p<0.001); time for review 35 minutes vs 45 minutes (p=0.019).

PMID:34632079.other_findings: An ED orthopaedic trauma fast-track pathway was introduced alongside the VFC; 88% and 92% of suspected fracture patients were treated in fast-track rooms. Median VFC review time was 9 minutes then 7 minutes per patient.

PMID:40622227.setting: Nationwide Dutch Hip Fracture Audit registry covering 66 hospitals

cycle1.result: Mortality 9.1% at 30 days, 15% at 90 days and 26% at 1 year. Logistic regression was preferred, with test-set c-statistics of 0.82 (30-day), 0.81 (90-day) and 0.80 (1-year).

PMID:40622227.other_findings: Registry-based machine learning prediction study, not an audit. ASA class, age and sex were the strongest predictors.

PMID:37818507.setting: Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust, a major trauma centre in north-west England; rib fixation by orthopaedic surgeons with the multidisciplinary Chest Injuries Group

cycle1.result: Mean 4.1 days from ED to rib fixation, critical care LOS 12.7 days, overall hospital LOS 29.1 days; mortality 3.3% (one death). In the matched cohort comparison, mortality was 36.7% conservative vs 3.3% rib fixation (p=0.001).

PMID:37818507.intervention: No specific intervention described; the re-audit reviewed the next cohort of rib fixation patients as the service developed.

cycle2.result: Mean 2.1 days from ED to rib fixation, critical care LOS 7.5 days and overall hospital LOS 20.7 days (LOS based on 17 patients); no deaths and no fixation-related complications.

PMID:37818507.other_findings: Matched cohort outcome study plus retrospective re-audit without a stated standard. No statistically significant differences in total hospital or ICU LOS between operative and conservative groups.

PMID:22400802.setting: Publicly funded community, sub-acute and acute podiatry services of Bendigo Health and Bendigo Community Health Services, regional Victoria

cycle1.result: University of Texas risk: no neuropathy 296 (51.4%), neuropathy 144 (25.0%), history of pathology 75 (13.0%), active pathology 61 (10.6%). New ulceration in 36 (6.3%); history of pathology predicted ulceration (OR 8.1, 95% CI 3.6 to 18.2, p<0.001).

PMID:22400802.other_findings: Described as a prospective clinical audit but is a descriptive epidemiological study with no standard. Higher risk was associated with longer diabetes duration, male sex and type 1 diabetes.

PMID:41781148.setting: Vancouver General Hospital arthroplasty service ('Short Term Accelerated Recovery' STAR programme)
PMID:41781148.standard: Aim of >80% successful same-day discharge among eligible primary THA patients without compromising safety (unscheduled 30-day hospital encounters)

cycle1.result: Standard cohort: 57/105 (54.3%) discharged same day; complications preventing same-day discharge 48 (45.7%); unscheduled 30-day hospital encounters 11 (10.5%).

PMID:41781148.intervention: Enhanced Recovery Canada recommendations: pre-emptive nausea prophylaxis (aprepitant, scopolamine patch), pre-emptive multimodal oral analgesia, and lidocaine epidural anaesthesia via a 'STAR Module' in the electronic order set, supported by STAR rounds, website posts and a video; then a switch to spinal lidocaine.

cycle2.result: Spinal lidocaine cohort: 80.6% discharged same day vs 54.3% (OR 3.4, 95% CI 1.34 to 8.66, p=0.0102).

PMID:41781148.other_findings: Combined ERC cohort (February 2021–August 2024, n=129): 96 (74.4%) same-day discharge (OR 2.51, p=0.0015), complications preventing discharge 33 (25.6%), 30-day encounters 12 (9.3%), not significantly different. Transient neurological symptoms in 3/33 (9%) spinal lidocaine patients; lack of evening physiotherapy limited reassessment.

PMID:31754810.topic: Participation in national hip fracture audit
PMID:31754810.setting: Survey of Dutch orthopaedic and trauma surgeons about the Dutch Hip Fracture Audit

cycle1.dates: Interviews 1 June 2017–8 November 2017; survey from November 2017
cycle1.result: Most agreed factors: staffing capacity for data collection (95.1%), automated data import (95.1%), financial support from hospital board (94.1%). Lower participation with academic hospital (OR 0.15, 95% CI 0.04–0.52) and orthopaedic surgeon (OR 0.30, 95% CI 0.10–0.90); data sharing with external parties associated with active participation (OR 3.19, 95% CI 1.14–8.95).

PMID:31754810.other_findings: Survey of opinion rather than an audit; 51 (46.8%) respondents reported active participation (≥80% of patients registered).

PMID:38024093.setting: Foot and ankle orthopaedic telephone clinic, York Hospital, a district general hospital

cycle1.result: Discharged 20 (19%); further face-to-face follow-up 52 (50%); further phone consult 12 (12%); did not attend 17 (17%); scans requested 5 (5%); listed for operation 2 (2%).

PMID:38024093.intervention: Orthopaedic clinician-led triage to select patients for telephone clinic.

cycle2.result: Discharged 44 (30%, p=0.030); further face-to-face follow-up 59 (40%, p=0.053); further phone consult 31 (21%, p=0.026); did not attend 13 (9%, p=0.033); scans requested 18 (12%, p=0.023); listed for operation 6 (4%, p=0.172).

PMID:38024093.other_findings: Described as a clinical audit but no explicit standard or target was stated. Among trauma patients alone, differences were not significant.
